description: Make a Java app's new copies start in about a second instead of several: each version is saved, started, when it is published, and every new copy starts from that save (a Spring app's first visitor waited 6.1 s before and about 1 s after). THIS COSTS MONEY BY EXISTING, at cost price: the platform charges exactly what AWS charges for keeping the save, plus the card fee on the credit, and makes nothing on it. It is paid from the account's Uarpie credit as it is used: by the hour while it is on (about $8.73 a month for a 2,048 MB app), each deploy's first three hours at once, and a few hundredths of a cent for each copy started. Call with no `on` to read the setting and the price (`estimate`), show the person the monthly price, and get a yes before turning it on. Java apps only, kept, on a paid plan with a spending limit above $0 and credit above $0 (otherwise refused, and the result's `blocker` or the error's `fix` says what is missing); not together with busy hours. Turning it off is always allowed. On a live app the change rolls out as a settings-only version, which takes about a minute longer than usual while the save is made.

on.description: true turns it on, false off. Leave out to read the setting and the price.

project.description: Project id (prj_…) or the app's name (slug). Defaults to the project in deploy.json in the current directory.
